maintainer_vibe: Process-driven volunteer moderators who enforce compliance with written policies. A GitHub Actions bot handles initial checklist and branch validation. Human maintainers intervene only for substantive issues: PR title convention violations, AI-generated content, or PRs targeting issues not yet open for contribution. Communication is direct and policy-referenced rather than conversational.
pr_guidelines: PR titles must follow the conventional commits format: type(scope): description, with description under 30 characters. Types are fix, feat, refactor, docs. Seen enforced by maintainer feedback on PR #69544 where imsomilg wrote: 'Please follow freeCodeCamp's convention for PR title.'

The PR description must include a genuinely completed contribution checklist. A GitHub Actions bot automatically comments when the checklist is missing or incomplete, as seen on PRs #69544 and #69746 where the bot listed all four required checklist items.

PRs must be opened from a dedicated feature branch (not the fork's main branch), targeting freeCodeCamp's main branch from a fork. The bot on PR #69748 explicitly warned: 'We recommend opening pull requests from a dedicated branch rather than your main branch.'
raw_summary: freeCodeCamp runs a high-volume repository (454,616 stars, 46,050 forks) with a volunteer-driven review process. A GitHub Actions bot enforces initial PR compliance: checklist completion, conventional commit title format, and dedicated branch usage. Human maintainers (imsomilg, plamoni, a2937) intervene for substantive issues and consistently cite written policies from the FAQ and contributing guide. Three key maintainer behaviors emerge from recent closed PRs: direct correction of PR title convention violations, immediate rejection of AI-generated contributions (PRs #69746 and #69748 were both closed for Claude Code attribution), and enforcement of the rule that PRs must target issues labeled help wanted or first timers only. The FAQ explicitly states AI-generated comments and responses will not be engaged with. Stale PRs are closed after inactivity with a brief 'Closed due to inactivity~' comment. The repository uses a deprioritized label for low-effort submissions and directs contributors to Discord or the community forum for questions rather than pinging maintainers. Issue quality is guided by templates that require detail, and linked issues must be open for contribution before PRs are accepted.
maintainer_persona: Policy-enforcing volunteer moderators. They automate initial review compliance via a bot, then apply written rules directly when escalating to human review. They reject AI-generated content firmly, close stale PRs casually, and redirect questions to community channels rather than engaging in back-and-forth.
top_dos: Follow the conventional commit PR title format (type[scope]: description under 30 chars) and include a genuinely completed PR checklist in the description
Open PRs from a dedicated feature branch targeting freeCodeCamp main, confirm local testing, and include Playwright integration tests for behavioral changes
Only submit PRs against issues labeled help wanted or first timers only; verify the issue is open for contribution before starting work
top_donts: Do not edit files directly through GitHub's web editor; all changes must come from a fork on a dedicated feature branch
Do not submit AI-generated content in PR descriptions, comments, or responses; the FAQ states maintainers will not engage with AI-generated replies
Do not @mention maintainers or reviewers; use the freeCodeCamp Community Discord channel or forum instead

deep_sections.title: What Contributors Actually Say
deep_sections.body: The contributor base is mixed between first-time participants and repeat contributors. PR #69544 by sultan-web22 included a checklist in the description but used a non-conventional title ('fix: added headers to user psuedo-class'), prompting imsomilg to write 'Please follow freeCodeCamp's convention for PR title.' PR #69746 by aqibali12 included a detailed root-cause analysis and test plan but was flagged for being generated with Claude Code. PR #69748 by Iitian001 targeted an issue not yet open for contribution and was also Claude Code generated. Contributors who follow conventions and avoid AI attributions receive no direct maintainer feedback beyond bot automation, suggesting that compliance with the checklist and title format is the primary filter for first review.

deep_sections.title: Hidden Friction Signals
deep_sections.body: Three friction points are visible in recent closed PRs: (1) The deprioritized label (seen on PR #69748) marks submissions as low-effort, reducing maintainer attention. (2) PRs targeting issues not yet open for contribution are closed immediately regardless of code quality, as plamoni noted on PR #69746: 'The related issue has not yet been opened for contribution, so we are not accepting PRs for it.' (3) AI-generated attribution in PR descriptions triggers a policy-based closure, as a2937 wrote on PR #69748, quoting the FAQ that maintainers will not engage with AI-generated content. The GitHub Actions bot's checklist and branch enforcement creates a two-layer gate: automation catches formatting issues, then human maintainers escalate policy violations.

deep_sections.title: Unwritten Rules
deep_sections.body: Beyond the written contributing guide, three norms govern success: (1) PR titles must match the conventional commits spec with a scope, as demonstrated by the maintainer correction on PR #69544. (2) The contributing guide states 'Following the guidelines carefully earns you the respect of fellow maintainers and saves everyone time,' signaling that procedural compliance is valued over raw code quality alone. (3) Stale PRs are closed casually with 'Closed due to inactivity~' (from imsomilg on PR #69544), suggesting a 21-day inactivity threshold after a status: waiting update label is applied. Contributors should expect automated bot feedback first, with human review reserved for issues that pass the initial compliance filter.
